text: POWER SYSTEMS STUDY During the Detailed Design phase, a study will be performed to set design requirements for mainline valve sites. Power required at each site shall be determined and appropriate source(s) for that power will be designed. At sites where the valve will be operated manually, solar power may be the best choice for the instrumentation and communication required. At sites where the valve will be operated by an actuator, each site will be evaluated for source requirements and designed accordingly. 11.3 BACKUP POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM Utility Power at each facility (i.e., MLV sites) will be evaluated on a case‐by‐case basis. If utility power is not economically available, sites shall be designed with local solar generation and battery storage. Page 17 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 11.4 INSTRUMENTATION DESIGN Pressure and temperature indication will be provided at sites, including pressure indication on both sides of all mainline valves and on all trap barrels. Where power and SCADA are available, indicating transmitters shall be installed for remote monitoring. Indicating transmitters may be installed at sites without utility power or actuation requirements if determined necessary for monitoring and control of the system; this determination shall be made in consultation with the OES Automation and Controls lead and in consideration of the control and leak detection system needs. 12 SCADA SYSTEM SCADA system design is beyond the scope of the Pipeline DBM. However, instrumentation specified for remotely monitored sites such as certain launchers, receivers, and RCV’s (remote controlled valves) shall be compatible with the overall SCADA system design and communications design. 12.1 LEAK DETECTION 49 CFR 195.134 requires leak detection that complies with the requirements in 195.444 for hazardous liquid pipelines transporting liquid in single phase (without gas in the liquid). New computational pipeline monitoring (CPM) leak detection system will be designed in accordance with the requirements in section 4.2 of API RP 1130. 12.2 FIELD LOCATIONS 12.2.1 CP Rectifiers Rectifiers shall be powered with utility power. Rectifiers shall be located and sized accordingly to align with existing utility power. Solar power will not be considered for rectifiers. 12.2.2 Block Valves Control RCV’s (remote controlled valves) shall be compatible with the overall SCADA system design and communications design. They will be triggered by human action at the Control Center and or by human actions at the mainline valve site. Some valves (e.g., smaller valves in non‐HCA areas) may not be RCV’s and also may not have motorized actuators. Motorized valve actuation will be dictated by the HCA analysis and EFRD study. 13 SECURITY All above ground pipeline components shall be fenced at a minimum with locking gate access. Access control, intrusion detection, monitoring, and other physical security considerations shall be provided in the detailed design of each above ground site.
